newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends down on commercial, local selling.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends down on commercial, local selling.

text.p: WCE canola futures closed lower on local and commercial selling linked to a bearish U.S. Department of Agriculture crop report, traders said.

"Our weakness is tied to the U.S. markets and the USDA report," a trader said. Cargill sold July canola and bought November while locals were agressive sellers all day and hedge sales increased. Crushers bought 600 July in continued trade to cover last week's 30,000 canola oil sale to China.
July WCE futures crush margin fell to -11.02 Monday from -2.75 Friday. About 700 July-Nov spread at $38, May-July $2. Volume was 5,450 lots, or 109,000 tonnes, with 430 hedge lots.
Japan bought 2,000-4,000 tonnes overnight, sources said.
July canola lost $1.70 to $425.60, November down $2.80 at $387.80. July flax rose $0.40 to $332.60 as PCTS bought while November fell $1.90 to $320.60, traders said.
"Locals covered shorts in the feed grains ahead of tomorrow's StatsCan report," a feed grain trader said.
Statistics Canada is scheduled to release its March 31 grain and oilseed stocks report at 0730 CDT/1230 GMT.
May western barley lost $1 to $135.50, July fell $1.60 to $135.60 as PCTS, UGG sold to LFG, traders said. July-Oct spread at $1. Volume 375 lots.
Oats and peas did not trade.
July feed wheat lost $2.20 to $160.40 by the close and October slipped $2 to $162.90 on commercials selling to locals. About 50 Oct-Dec spread at $1, 25 Dec-Mar $3.50.
(All prices in Canadian dollars/tonne except oats, peas).
